content: The National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine (NCCAM) is a United States government agency. It is committed to investigating complementary and alternative healing practices through rigorous scientific methods, training researchers in complementary and alternative medicine (CAM), and disseminating reliable information to both the public and healthcare professionals. NCCAM is one of the 27 institutes and centers that comprise the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which operates under the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) of the federal government. The NIH itself is one of eight agencies within the Public Health Service (PHS) under DHHS. NCCAM was originally established in October 1991 as the Office of Alternative Medicine and was restructured as NCCAM in October 1998. Its mission is to explore CAM practices scientifically, train CAM researchers, and provide authoritative information to the public and professionals. NCCAM funds research into CAM practices, including clinical trials to evaluate their efficacy. It also supports basic and clinical science research projects by awarding grants nationally and internationally. Additionally, NCCAM conducts its own clinical and laboratory-based studies on the NIH campus in Bethesda, Maryland. The center focuses on four primary areas: 1. Research: NCCAM supports clinical and basic science research projects in CAM by awarding grants and conducting its own studies. These efforts aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of CAM practices. 2. Research Training and Career Development: NCCAM provides grants to support training and career development opportunities for predoctoral, postdoctoral, and career researchers in the field of CAM. 3. Outreach: NCCAM sponsors conferences, educational programs, and exhibits. It operates an information clearinghouse to respond to inquiries and provide information. It also maintains a website, publishes printed materials, and organizes town meetings across the United States. 4. Integration: NCCAM works to integrate scientifically validated CAM practices into conventional medicine. This includes publishing research results, studying methods to incorporate evidence-based CAM practices into standard medical care, and supporting programs to develop models for including CAM in the curricula of medical, dental, and nursing schools. NCCAM was formally established by Congress in 1998. It is organized into several divisions and offices, including the Office of the Director, the Executive Office, the Division of Extramural Activities, and the Division of Intramural Research. Specific offices within these divisions include the Office of Grants Management, the Office of Scientific Review, the Office of Clinical and Regulatory Affairs, the Office of International Health Research, and the Office of Special Populations. The Division of Intramural Research includes specialized units such as the Endocrine Section, the Diabetes Unit, and the Oncology Program. Critics of NCCAM argue that despite its stated goals, the center and its predecessor, the Office of Alternative Medicine, have spent over $800 million on research since 1991 without scientifically demonstrating the efficacy of any single alternative medicine method or declaring any alternative treatment effective. Additional facts about NCCAM include: It offers a multi-level peer-review process for grant applications, involving scientists, practitioners, and public representatives. It receives advice and recommendations from the National Advisory Council for Complementary and Alternative Medicine and from federal representatives on the Transagency CAM Coordinating Committee. Its website hosts databases such as CAM on PubMed, a subset of the National Library of Medicine's PubMed, which provides access to journal citations related to CAM. The NCCAM Clearinghouse serves as the public's primary contact point for scientifically based information on CAM and details about NCCAM's activities. The information provided here is based on NCCAM's publication (No. D158, June 2002), which is in the public domain and not copyrighted.
